overview.title: Overview
overview.body:
# Overview
Chess is a two-player strategy game played on an 8×8 board.

Each player controls an army of pieces with different movement rules.

Players take turns moving one piece at a time, trying to attack and eventually trap the opponent’s king.

goal.title: Goal of the Game
goal.body:
# Goal
The goal is to checkmate the opponent’s king.

A king is checkmated when:

- it is under attack
- and there is no legal move to escape

You do not win by capturing the king directly.

board.title: The Board
board.body:
# The Board
The chess board has 64 squares arranged in an 8×8 grid.

Squares alternate between light and dark colors.

Important setup rule:

- the bottom-right square from each player's perspective should be a light square

Rows are called **ranks**.
Columns are called **files**.

setup.title: Setup
setup.body:
# Setup
Each player begins with:

- 1 king
- 1 queen
- 2 rooks
- 2 bishops
- 2 knights
- 8 pawns

The second row is filled with pawns.

Back-row order from left to right:

rook, knight, bishop, queen, king, bishop, knight, rook

Important:

- the queen starts on her own color
- white moves first

turn-structure.title: Turn Structure
turn-structure.body:
# Turn Structure
Players alternate turns.

On your turn:

1. Choose one of your pieces.
2. Move it according to its movement rules.
3. Optionally capture an opponent piece.

You may not make a move that leaves your king in check.

piece-movement.title: How Pieces Move
piece-movement.body:
# How Pieces Move
## King
Moves one square in any direction.

## Queen
Moves any number of squares horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.

## Rook
Moves any number of squares horizontally or vertically.

## Bishop
Moves any number of squares diagonally.

## Knight
Moves in an L-shape:

- two squares in one direction
- then one square sideways

Knights can jump over pieces.

## Pawn
Usually moves forward one square.

From its starting position, a pawn may move forward two squares.

Pawns capture diagonally forward one square.

capturing.title: Capturing Pieces
capturing.body:
# Capturing Pieces
A piece captures by moving onto a square occupied by an opponent piece.

The captured piece is removed from the game.

Most pieces capture using the same movement they normally use.

Pawns are special:

- they move forward
- but capture diagonally

check.title: Check
check.body:
# Check
A king is in **check** if an opponent piece is attacking it.

If your king is in check, you must respond immediately.

Ways to escape check:

- move the king
- block the attack
- capture the attacking piece

You may never ignore check.

checkmate.title: Checkmate
checkmate.body:
# Checkmate
Checkmate happens when:

- your king is in check
- and there is no legal way to escape

The game ends immediately.

The player delivering checkmate wins.

special-rules.title: Special Rules
special-rules.body:
# Special Rules
## Castling
Castling is a special move involving the king and a rook.

Conditions:

- neither piece has moved before
- no pieces between them
- the king is not currently in check
- the king does not move through check

The king moves two squares toward the rook, and the rook moves next to the king.

## Promotion
When a pawn reaches the far side of the board, it is promoted.

Usually it becomes a queen.

## En Passant
A special pawn capture that can happen immediately after a pawn moves two squares forward.

draws.title: Draws
draws.body:
# Draws
Chess can end in a draw in several ways.

Common examples:

## Stalemate
A player has no legal move, but their king is not in check.

## Agreement
Both players agree to a draw.

## Insufficient Material
Neither side has enough pieces to force checkmate.

## Repetition
The same position repeats multiple times.

## Fifty-Move Rule
Too many moves occur without pawn movement or captures.

basic-principles.title: Basic Principles
basic-principles.body:
# Basic Principles
Beginner strategy ideas:

- Control the center.
- Develop pieces early.
- Do not move the same piece repeatedly without reason.
- Castle to protect your king.
- Try to keep pieces defended.
- Think about what your opponent threatens.

Chess is often about balancing:

- king safety
- piece activity
- material advantage
- long-term positioning

first-turn-summary.title: First Turn Summary
first-turn-summary.body:
# First Turn Summary
On your turn:

1. Choose one piece.
2. Make a legal move.
3. Capture if possible.
4. Ensure your king is not left in check.

Beginner reminders:

- Try to develop knights and bishops early.
- Protect your king.
- Watch for attacks on undefended pieces.
- Before every move, ask:
  - What changed?
  - What is my opponent threatening?
